topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and defines the learning objectives regarding cancer etiology and carcinogens.

topics.label: Concepts of Cancer Etiology, Genetic Predisposition, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore what cancer is at a cellular level, balancing the interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations, bad luck, inherited predispositions, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Specific Carcinogenic Agents and Mechanisms of Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific biological and chemical carcinogens—including infectious pathogens, aflatoxins, UV radiation, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, TCDD, and aromatic amines—and the distinct biochemical mechanisms by which they induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation, Promotion, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between tumor initiators and promoters, highlighting non-mutagenic drivers like chronic inflammation, the two-stage model of carcinogenesis, and the impact of host developmental timing on cancer susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the laboratory, genomic, in vivo, and epidemiological approaches used to identify mutational signatures, assess mutagenicity, and evaluate the carcinogenicity and risk of environmental exposures.
